title: Four 2024 CRW composite maps kept weekly maxima but did not identify the seasonal Alert fraction
abstract: We test the meaning of NOAA Coral Reef Watch four-month summary maps. All 2,985,160 values checked in ten probability-level maps for four fixed 2024 issues equal the maximum included weekly level. We derive count bounds for the seasonal Alert fraction among the 28 long-run members when weekly ensembles shrink from 112 to 49 to 28. The method accounts for unknown removed-member events and quantile ranks. Across 74,629 ocean cells at 35 S to 35 N, 73.0-91.8% have Alert 1+ seasonal fraction ranges at least 25 percentage points wide under either tested integer rank rule. Mean widths are 64.9-87.2 points with floor ranks. A changing ensemble also prevents a general lower-bound interpretation of the largest weekly fraction for the common-member seasonal target. These are information bounds over arbitrary binary paths, not measured risk errors or confidence limits. Only four issues, coarse rank maps, assumed common membership and no physical path constraints limit the result. We provide source hashes, retrieval code, a proof, exhaustive small-case checks and aggregate evidence.

display.caption: Seasonal Alert fraction ranges allowed by the weekly rank maps and retained-member assumptions. This is information uncertainty, not a confidence interval.
